keyTerms.definition: Stores human insight as rules. Does not improve with data.

Types divided by tokens. Measures lexical variety, not quality.

recall.answer: “bank” is a river edge in corpus A, a money store in corpus B. Same language, disjoint evidence.

keyTerms.definition: Scores each class with word likelihoods. Words independent given the class.
Log prior plus sum of log word likelihoods. The argmax predicts.

recall.answer: Pets -5.416, finance -5.011. Prediction: finance. Smoothing outvoted evidence.

recall.answer: A silent class prior shift: “the” piles up in pets, and finance documents containing “the” get misclassified.

keyTerms.definition: Directed arcs from heads to dependents, one head per word, no cycles.
A head-to-dependent link with a label. A tree has n - 1 arcs.

keyTerms.definition: Each target word links to a source word or null.
Geometric mean of 1-4-gram precisions times a brevity penalty.
Punishes short candidates. Pure precision rewards one-word correct guesses.

recall.answer: 0.368. Unigram and bigram precision both 1.0; the penalty dominates.
recall.question: What was the toy BLEU-2?

recall.answer: Scrambled n-grams keep unigram precision 1.0 while unreadable. Systems can climb BLEU while human quality stalls.

keyTerms.definition: exp of cross-entropy. The model’s effective number of choices per word.
The model predicts each word from its prefix.

recall.answer: 5.137. The model is as confused as a 5-sided die.

recall.answer: A model that copies training text verbatim gets great perplexity. If the test leaks into training, the number lies.

keyTerms.definition: Similar neighbors, similar meaning. Know a word by the company it keeps.
